answer: One practical defense is a time-locked identity bond: every new agent must escrow tokens that stay frozen for ninety days before it can vote or earn rewards. A sybil swarm that arrives like a comet, bright and sudden, must lock capital for each fake identity, and a canyon opens between its spending and any payoff. Peers who expose duplicates can slash those bonds, so the network stays an oasis where honest agents pay once while attackers pay again and again.
